notes.title: Achievements and Iron Will mode
notes.content:
Seekers of complex logistics and production challenges,

I am pleased to announce the completion of achievement testing.

In addition to them, I added the [b]"Iron Will"[/b] mode to the game, which gives the epic attainments [b]"Simply Genius 1/2/3"[/b]. To unlock them, you need to complete the game by simultaneously fulfilling up to 15 conditions out of 18 (i.e. 3 can be skipped).

Another important change: [b]space teleporters no longer have a range limit of 5 sectors[/b], and therefore it is now possible to easily build an entire logistics system using only teleporters (but the cost of teleportation has increased from 2 energy units to 3x for each sector between the sender and recipient).

Also, to improve the comfort of the game, the system for selecting the type of resources required for planet upgrades has been improved. I hope it becomes even more enjoyable to play!

And, please don’t forget about the [b]disassembler mode[/b] if you have enough experience in the game and haven’t tried it. It is radically different from other gameplay modes. Planets provide you with ready-made, composite resources that need to be disassembled into their component parts using chains of disassemblers (each of which has an unlimited operating speed), and then reassemble these parts into those finished products that require a colony to function and develop.

Have fun!

TaosX

notes.title: Game Release
notes.content:
[h1]Release version changes.[/h1]

[h2]Rapid construction tools.[/h2]

It is now possible to install a fully configured and piped machine in just a few clicks. It also became possible to build an entire production chain from an existing machine to a required resource.

[h2]New technology tree.[/h2]

Technologies have been reorganized into a tree structure, with direct dependencies on all previous technologies. Added the ability to add all previous technologies to the research queue with one click.

[h2]Obtaining memory for research.[/h2]

Now, in addition to capturing sectors and leveling up planets and deposits, memory is added for reaching the levels of the total population.

[h2]Alternative research mode (optional hard mode).[/h2]

In this mode, the player cannot directly select the research target. After increasing the level of AI, it is proposed to choose the opening of one of the three technologies (taking into account their dependence on the technology tree). This makes it more difficult to achieve in-game goals, especially when combined with other high difficulty options.

[h2]Direct docking of ships and stations.[/h2]

It became possible to connect a ship through pipes to a station or another ship for a direct transfer of resources without the cost of energy for teleportation.

[h2]Autologic "Waypoints".[/h2]

To automate logistics using direct docking, the player can set movement points for any ship, with different types of waiting (loading, unloading, while the ore is being mined on the asteroid). This logic gives 100% control over logistics and allows you to implement visualized production chains of any complexity.

[h2]Orbital elevator.[/h2]

Every station above a habitable planet can use an orbital elevator to transport resources back and forth without the need for a transport ship to hyperjump to the planet.

[h2]Logistics system.[/h2]

The player can use three independent tools to build the logistics system: routes and transport ships, teleportation relays (within 5 sectors) and direct docking along with waypoints. Any combination is also possible. 

[h2]Shipyard logic.[/h2]

Allows you to organize the automated construction of specified ships non-stop, until the selected fleet size is reached.

[h2]Logic of the ammunition carrier.[/h2]

A transport ship with this logic will deliver ammunition directly to warships.

[h2]Fleet management.[/h2]

In a special map mode, the player can issue commands simultaneously to all ships of a sector to attack another sector.

[h2]Living metal.[/h2]

Technologies for the production of living metals (in nano-assembler) and their composites are available. Living metals have resistances to various types of damage similar to ordinary metals, but when damaged, they regenerate by consuming energy from batteries.

[h2]Behavior of enemy factions.[/h2]

Now when an enemy faction is attacked by an enemy or the aggression threshold set in the options is reached, the faction will gradually start attacking and capturing the player's sectors. The less sectors a faction has left, the harder it fights.

[h2]The colony produces resources only after supplying the requested resources (optional hard mode).[/h2]

In the main mode, the colony starts producing resources immediately. In the same mode, you first need to research, produce and deliver the resource of constant demand requested by the colony. This is where asteroid mining becomes critical.

[h2]Other new options.[/h2]

Now it is possible to customize the gameplay completely to your taste. You can enable or disable orders to upgrade the planet and its deposits. You can make the map completely open at the start. You can make all technologies available right away, or you can start with enough memory for all research. You can choose between fast gameplay or a long run. You can enable or disable the multiplier of energy consumption from the number of machines used.

[h2]Difficulty modes.[/h2]

Added seven preset difficulty modes from easy to impossible. You can also manually activate any set of options.

[h2]New machine: nuclear reactor.[/h2]

Size 5x5. Consumes uranium rods and coolant.

[h2]New machine: nano assembler.[/h2]

Size 3x5. Consumes metal and nanites. Produces living metal.

[h2]New machine: disassembler.[/h2]

Size 7x7. Disassembles resources into raw materials.

[h2]Resources.[/h2]

Added new types of resources. Rebalanced production recipes. The logic of production has been straightened out: machines consume one unit of resources and energy, and produce another unit of resource.

Enjoy!

notes.title: Gameplay Rebalancing
notes.content:
[h1]Hello everyone![/h1]

I'm happy to announce that I've finished rebalancing the gameplay ([b]EXPERIMENTAL BRANCH[/b]).

[b]Why it was needed:[/b] Players have repeatedly reported that even at the highest difficulty levels, technologies are researched too easily and lose interest because of this. At the same time, the easy difficulty levels should remain so that novice players can get comfortable.

[h2]Two options that significantly increase the complexity:[/h2]

1. Alternative research mode.
2. Planetary deposits consume resources.

The essence of the [b]alternate research mode[/b] is that you can't directly research any technology. When the AI ​​gains enough experience to level up, you are offered a choice of three technologies for which all predecessors have been researched. This adds an element of unpredictability and makes the choice much more meaningful. By choosing one of the technologies, you reduce the chance of the roll of the other two. Each subsequent technology requires more memory than the previous one. In contrast to the normal mode, the memory deficit is felt more strongly. In the face of severe limitations in available memory, this leads to situations of difficult choice. Go for nuclear power to end the global energy shortage, or take on more powerful munitions to push back the attacking faction, even if the next chance for nuclear power comes in many rolls?

The second option "[b]Planetary deposits consume resources[/b]" makes it necessary to use asteroids to the full extent. A planet does not automatically start resource mining immediately after its capture, until you have supplied it with resources of constant demand. At the beginning of the game, there will be a total lack of resources. They will need to be distributed literally bit by bit. Until you level up the planet, the exchange will go 1:1 / 1:2. In the middle and end of the game, you need to be careful not to cascade production shutdown. And if this happens, there is a chance your management talent to restart your incredibly complex production mechanism.

The harder the game, the sweeter the win, right?

What has also been made more difficult: 

[h2]Faction battles.[/h2]

In this game, the emphasis is not on manual control and single battles, but on the economic component of the war and the automatic control of fleets leading several battles at once. For this, there is the [b]logic of a shipyard[/b] (non-stop construction of ships), [b]ammo carriers[/b], and the [b]fleet management tool[/b] so that you can send many ships from one sector to another at once.

Factions, on their part, after the start of the war, build attack fleets on their planets and send them to capture your sectors. The fewer sectors remain under their control, the faster they prepare new ships. [b]The closer you get to destroying a faction, the harder it gets.[/b]

[h3]What you need to win:[/h3]

1. Produce armor with the correct type of resistance, depending on the faction's weapon type.
2. Produce the most advanced ammo of the type that deals the most damage to the armor of the selected faction.
3. Organize fast and uninterrupted production in the required volumes.
4. Have enough energy to capture enemy sectors.
5. Strategically choose sectors to attack, considering that a faction becomes more aggressive the fewer sectors it has left.

[b]Recent changes have made the yellow faction the most difficult to defeat.[/b] Most likely, you will need to deeply research the technologies of lasers and living metal in order to win. These technologies are the most difficult to obtain.

Ammo has been rebalanced to make [b]early fights[/b] viable.

If you have a lot of experience in the game and are looking for a challenge worthy of your abilities, [b]I recommend the "Master" setting[/b]. The additional option "[b]Long Run[/b]" increases the difficulty even more.

But don't limit yourself. The game can be assembled brick by brick from a large number of settings. 

[b]Want faster gameplay?[/b] Disable upgrades of planets and deposits. 

[b]Do you want to build a lot of machines and not experience resource constraints?[/b] Turn on "[b]Abundant Resources[/b]". 

[b]Are you for peace and hate violence?[/b] Add "[b]Peaceful Mode[/b]" to "Master" difficulty mode (maybe with "Long Run" if you like). It's your game. 

Enjoy!

And please let me know what you think of the latest changes.

Always yours,
TaosX

P.S. [b]How to activate the experimental branch:[/b] 
Right click on the game in the Steam Library -> Properties -> Betas -> Update 2.1

notes.title: Update 2.1 is ready for testing!
notes.content:
[b]Hi Friends![/b]

That day has Finally arrived. Update 2.1 is ready for testing on the EXPERIMENTAL branch.

[h1]New features:[/h1]

1. [b]New building tools[/b] that allow you to create a fully connected and configured machine in a few clicks. Or even an entire production chain.

2. [b]New technology tree. New resources for production. New production machines.[/b]

3. [b]Game options[/b] to create a set of rules just for you. From [b]easy and fast paced[/b] gameplay to a [b]mind-bending puzzle[/b] game where every step counts.

4. [b]Large-scale battles[/b] in which the economy is of great importance. Enemies will press on your borders incessantly if the war is started. New tools will help you with this: [b]shipyard logic[/b] that builds combat ships non-stop; [b]fleet management mode[/b], which allows you to move many warships between sectors at a time; [b]regenerating living armor[/b].

5. [b]Direct docking[/b] of ships and stations. Together with the [b]auto-logic "Waypoints"[/b], you can build logistics chains of incredible complexity.

Let me know what you think.

Yours sincerely,
TaosX

[*] The tech tree has been redesigned in vein of Update 2, but with some significant improvements based on feedback.

[*] Improved fluid system in several areas. For example, it is now possible to connect machines without a tank in the middle.
[*] All new combat system improvements have been moved: fleet management, faction aggressive behavior, single ship logic.

[/olist]

After that, I will open a new experimental branch.

Thank you for playing and sharing your ideas!

Fixed map zoom on specific screen resolutions like 1200x1000.

Hello everyone!

I recently made Update 2 available for testing on the experimental branch. The goal of the update was to make the game more beginner-friendly (while adding new content). After discussion with the brilliant community on the Steam forum and Discord channel, I decided not to replace the current version with the Update 2 build, but to include the best features and continue development in the direction that was approved by the community. 

(However, you may find Update 2 enjoyable to play if you enjoy fast-paced gameplay. To try it, activate it in the experimental branch: Properties/Betas/experimental3 0.4.0)

[b]This update contains some visual and quality of life improvements.[/b]

Added planet terraformation visualization.
Added new music tracks.

Quality of life:

Added button to change the min batch size of all routes at once.
Added global map zoom.
Added an opaque mesh in build mode to make it easier to build against a bright background.
Improved transparent wall visuals.
Added menu option to disable edge scrolling.
Added menu option to turn on the sounds of production machines in the distance.
Decreases the volume of the laser gun's firing sound.
Added text search in object/tech selection window.
Added text search in the ship/station list window.
Added ship roles filter in the structures list window.
Added 'move ship aside' menu option.
Added hotkey label to menu options (if available).
Updated F2 database view.
Improved construction cannon logic.
Enlarged the right notification panel. Redesigned notification icons.

Reduced the overall game size by almost 2 times due to the use of procedural planetary textures.

[b]Expect the following small updates:[/b]

New step by step tutorial.

A demo version.

Improvements to the combat system, including fleet management and mass building of ships with a new shipyard logic.
New machines and resources.
Living metals that regenerate after being damaged.

After all the features of Update 2 are implemented in the main branch, I will conduct another major experiment to improve the logistics system. I see a clear request to make the gameplay more challenging and visually rewarding. I would like to try to remove teleportation from the game (too simple) and introduce a new way to move resources: direct connection of a ship to a station. On the one hand, this will require more effort to organize resource flows (smart design of user stations and ships, manual binding of ships to certain positions). On the other hand, it can be a very visual and enjoyable process. Of course, as an experiment, a decision will be made based on your feedback.

Thanks for playing and have a nice day!

Please let me know if you find any bugs. I will be happy to fix them as soon as possible.

notes.title: Development Progress Report
notes.content:
Hello everyone! It has been a month since I started working on Update 1 and I would like to share the intermediate result.

After reading your feedback I decided not to cut any existing feature, but only to expand and improve.
[b]The route system remains in the game. [/b]You will be able to choose your own playstyle and to decide to use [b]routes[/b] or to rely on the new [b]teleportation logistics system[/b].
 
Here is a list of new features (it may change).
 
[h1]Economy [Done].[/h1]
[olist]
[*] Every colony will have a [b]constant demand[/b] for one resource type. If you build a production chain, it will bring you income forever. And you can always improve/expand the production to earn more.
[*] The number of colonizable planets will be increased.
[*] When a colony's population reaches certain limit, it will order some other resources to level up and to increase the consumption of the main resource.
[*] Raw resource deposits now require [b]scanning[/b] before harvesting. The cost is substantial, but it is a onetime payment.
[*] [b]Miners will not spend 50% of ore cost for harvesting[/b]. It will prevent the massive drain of energy credits by miners. It was a major annoyance for some players.
[*] Energy generation will be much faster. You will be able to generate power from raw carbon ore, from refined carbon and from oil.
[*] [b]Energy is no longer bought by Earth.[/b] But it is still possible to buy energy for credits.
[*] General production speed will increase x2, same as output of resource deposits.
[/olist]
	 
[h1]Tech research [Done].[/h1]
[olist]
[*] Suppling resources to colonies now do not bring XP.
[*] Techs are now unlocked and improved by research stations. They consume energy, as usual.
[*] A [b]research queue[/b] is implemented.
[*] [b]Memory chips[/b] are now required to store the data. Every memory chip stores 10 unlocks/upgrades.
[*] Every consequent memory chip costs more and more. Buying memory chips will be the main [b]money sink[/b]. But the upper cost is limited. At some point, the price will not raise anymore (it is related to the max possible earnings when you fully develop all your colonies). To unlock and upgrade the whole tech tree it will takes more than [b]500 levels[/b] (but it is not required to finish the game).
[/olist]
 
I tried several different approaches to economy, and this turned out to be the most viable solution.
To progress, you need both energy and credits. Now you have a [b]full control over credits spending[/b].
Your [b]money balance will always grow[/b], and you choose where to spend the money; how to improve your resource flow to get more credits per minute.
 
[h1]Module system (the main feature of the update) [Done].[/h1]
[olist]
[*] Module is a part of a ship or station which can be inserted into a blueprint or can be added to an existing ship or station.
[*] [b]Built-in modules[/b] will allow to compose a custom station (considering local supply and demand) fast and easy.
[*] Same as auto-stations, you choose an item to produce or store, than select one of module configurations (where input comes from and where the output goes to), place it and all of it machines/resource zones/tanks will be set automatically.
[*] The standard modules will fit into a grid of certain size, so you can easily connect different modules to each other.
[*] You can develop an unlimited number of your own modules and to share it via the [b]Steam Workshop [/b]same as blueprints.
[*] Modules are very convenient to start with a small station and expanding it later, or to create a custom production chain on the fly, not spending too much time to design the blueprint.
[/olist]
 
[h1]New machines.[/h1]
[olist]
[*] [b]Trade Hub [Done].[/b] A machine to teleport ores and liquids from the local planet surface and to sell final product to a local colony. An alternative to ship routes. Allows to maximize the usage of a deposit. It is an unlockable tech so you may skip it if you want.
[*] [b]Quantum Storage T1-T3 [Done].[/b] Stores 100-1000-10000 units of solid resources. Can be used in all types of trade interactions and mining.  A great way to make huge stocks of everything. An unlockable tech, so you may skip it and use only resource zones.
[*] [b]Teleportation Relay [WIP].[/b] Connects two neighboring stations. Allows to teleport items/liquids back and forth.
[*] [b]Construction Cannon [WIP].[/b] A mid-end game alternative to construction by robots. Much faster construction but requires more energy.
[/olist]
 
[b]Matter and anti-matter generators[/b] are in the plan but may be moved to the next update.
 
[h1]New items [WIP].[/h1]
[olist]
[*] [b]Final products:[/b] an oxygen generator, a portable power generator, a water purifier, a terraforming machine, and a work drone.
[*] [b]Intermediate products:[/b] CPU T1-T3, engine T1-T3.
[/olist]
 
I limited the number of new resources in this update to not to delay it too much. I am going to add more new items in every further update.
 
[b]When?[/b] As it usually happens in software development, it takes longer than expected. Some changes take much time to implement and fail after playtesting. But it is the price for search of a new, original gameplay.
 
I plan to put the update to the [b]Experimental branch before the end of the year.[/b] How long it will take to reach the main branch, depends on your feedback and the amount of the update refinement. 

As you may know, I am the single developer of the project. But I am completely devoted to it and working hard to bring you new cool features.
 
Thank you for your attention and have a great day!

notes.title: Update 1 Announcement
notes.content:
First, I would like to express sincere gratitude for all players who supports the game in the early stages of development. Basing of your feedback and ideas, I am going to rework the most important game system: economy and logistics. In a few weeks, you will get a test 0.3 version on the Experimental branch.

The main goal is to make game more complex and engaging, to raise replayability sky-high.

[b]What will change:[/b]
[olist]
[*] The cost of hyper jump will increase x100 times.
[*] Colonies will have constant (but upgradable) demand for 4 item types, depending on the sector quality. Once you built a production chain, it will bring you income forever.
[*] Stations will be interconnected with teleportation relays, able to sustain up to 10 resource flows.
[*] Only neighboring stations can be connected with teleportation relays.
[*] Trade hubs will be used to teleport raw ores & liquids from a planet and sell finished products to it.
[*] Instead of building standard stations from blueprints, you will be building a unique station in each sector, considering local demand and supply. In fact, you will be building one huge space station across the whole sector of the galaxy, solving a giant logistic puzzle with hundreds of live, visual resource flows.
[/olist]
[b]To assist you in that:[/b]
[olist]
[*] Instant building will be available (at x2 cost comparing to robot construction). 
[*] A modules library will be added. You will be able to design a specialized area of station or ship, to paste it to another blueprint or a live object.
[/olist]
All these changes will be moved to the main branch only if the build gets positive feedback from the community.

ETA: 2-3 months, may be more (much earlier on the Experimental branch).

notes.title: Steam Workshop Integration is Live!
notes.content:
[url=https://steamcommunity.com//workshop/browse?appid=919260]Final Upgrade Workshop[/url]

Now you can download ships and stations blueprints of other players!
Share your own beautiful creations!

File structure in the Blueprints folders changed: now every blueprint lies in a separate folder with the same name. Please, don't change file names manually OR make sure the directory name matches the *.bytes name. The game will move all your existing files to folders automatically.

[b]Steps to submit a blueprint:[/b]
1. Open it in game.
2. Click 'Send to Steam' button.
3. Select an appropriate tag and fill the description.
4. Hit 'Send'.

Note: sending a blueprint requires sign of Steam Workshop agreement.
You can do it here: [url=https://steamcommunity.com//workshop/browse?appid=919260]https://steamcommunity.com/workshop/workshoplegalagreement[/url]

You can edit you workshop item in a browser.
Note: changing the blueprint title on the Workshop page won't change it's in-game name.

Steps to download blueprints from the Workshop:
1. Visit [url=https://steamcommunity.com//workshop/browse?appid=919260]Final Upgrade Workshop[/url] in your browser.
2. Subscribe to one or many blueprints.
3. Run the game. It will be uploaded automatically and placed to your Blueprints folder. 

Note: you can make changes in the downloaded item. But it may be overwritten if the creator update it.
To avoid it, rename the blueprint or unsubscribe from it on the Workshop page.
*Unsubscribing from an item does not delete it in-game.

Please, let me know if you encounter any bugs or issues.

notes.title: Weekly Patch Notes
notes.content:
I'd like to thank you all for your support, your feedback and bugreports!

The first week after release was very intense for bug fixes and improvements.
I'm working hard to make the game as good as possible.

[b]Quality of Life Improvements:[/b]

Manually initiated harvest now does not changes tank / resource zone settings.

notes.title: Roadmap
notes.content:
After the release, we will have two types of update:

1) Minor bug fixes and existing feature improvement patches.
2) Major updates, once every few months. These will be called “Update 1”, “Update 2”, and so on, independently of the build number.

The update content will greatly depend on your feedback and suggestions.

Here are some [b]possible[/b] directions:
1.	New machines and T2 and T3 versions of existing machines
2.	New items to produce
3.	New weapons and damage types
4.	Shields
5.	New factions
6.	Bigger maps
7.	Bigger ships and stations
8.	Mega-structure building – jump gates, orbital lifts, planet deep-drilling machines, huge quantum computers
9.	Procedural planets (same 3D view as asteroids) – huge space to build a main base
10.	Modding support

The creation of every update will have several phases:
1) Experiments with the core game code to check the potential and performance of big features.
2) Offering the community several major options for the update and voting for the preferred options (democracy, yay!); we will add minor features to the list too.
3) Uploading to an experimental branch when the first iteration of the new build is ready.
4) Playtesting by you, and, when it is ready, uploading to the main branch.

So, this is just a beginning, and the possibilities are endless. A long road lies ahead (several years for sure).

I need your support. Join us today to make it happen!
